records.source_question: What fields appear on a sample invoice in this synthetic demo policy?
answer_facts: In the synthetic demo billing policy, a sample invoice lists an invoice reference, issue date, item subtotal, delivery fee, demo tax, discount, and total due. Total due equals subtotal plus delivery fee plus demo tax minus discount. This glossary does not retrieve an account invoice.

records.source_question: Which payment method labels does the synthetic demo policy recognize?
answer_facts: In the synthetic demo billing policy, the illustrative payment method labels are demo card and demo credit. The labels describe sample records only; this assistant cannot collect card details, update a method, or take payment.

records.source_question: Is an invoice the same as a payment receipt?
answer_facts: In the synthetic demo billing policy, an invoice states an amount due, while a payment receipt would confirm a separately verified recorded payment and its amount. An invoice alone does not prove payment; this demo has no payment-record integration or actual receipt verification.

records.source_question: What do the sample invoice charge lines mean?
answer_facts: In the synthetic demo billing glossary, item subtotal is merchandise before additions or reductions; delivery fee is a separate shipping charge; demo tax is an illustrative tax line; and discount reduces total due. The glossary cannot explain an individual account charge.

records.source_question: Does seeing two similar charge lines prove a duplicate payment?
answer_facts: No. Under the synthetic demo billing process, matching amounts or dates are clues for case review, not proof of a duplicate payment. A customer can describe the two synthetic charge references and dates for simulated Billing follow-up; the FAQ cannot verify transactions or decide a refund.

records.source_question: What do the sample delivery-stage labels mean?
